question:
[MCQ] Based on the video clip, what major optimization change is made when the view remains suboptimal, and what is the purpose?
A. Move the probe to a more posterior intercostal space to reduce rib shadowing and obtain a clearer view.
B. Have the patient take a deep inspiration and hold it to lower the diaphragm and improve the acoustic window.
C. Switch to a lower-frequency probe to increase penetration and improve visualization through overlying tissue.

inference_metadata.raw_response:
Answer: A
The video shows an initial view of the liver and gallbladder that is partially obscured by acoustic shadowing, likely from the ribs. The sonographer is seen manipulating the probe, sliding it across the skin. During this movement (around 00:02-00:05), the image becomes highly echogenic and disorganized, which is characteristic of scanning over the rib cage or lung interface. The action of sliding the probe to find a clear window between the ribs corresponds to moving to an intercostal space. This maneuver is performed to bypass the rib shadows and obtain a clearer acoustic window of the underlying structures. The black screen at the end likely represents lifting the probe to reposition it to a more posterior intercostal space.

B. A major vascular landmark (aorta/IVC) at the margin to re-center the target and estimate its depth from the midline

inference_metadata.raw_response:

The operator slides the probe laterally (to the right on the screen) to move the transducer into an intercostal space or subcostal window. By surveying the edge of the field for this rib-induced shadowing, the operator can adjust the probe angle and position to minimize the artifact and obtain a clear view of the underlying parenchyma, as seen in the later frames (0:06-0:14).
